title: Why Can't You Say the COLOUR, Not the Word? 🎨
description:
Say the ink colour of each word out loud, not the word. Did you trip? Reading is so practised that your brain reads every word you see whether you want it to or not, so the word barges into your mouth before the colour gets a turn. Coloured squiggles with no words? Easy. Little kids who can't read yet barely trip at all, but kids who have just learned to read (around ages 7 to 9) trip the hardest of anyone, and it eases off as you grow up. Reading the words instead is easy: the ink colour hardly slows you down. It's called the Stroop effect, after John Ridley Stroop, who published it in 1935, spent 45 years teaching at a college in Nashville and, according to his son, died in 1973 not knowing how famous it had become.
